sources.title: Vous voyagez avec des sommes, des titres ou des valeurs d'un montant egal ou superieur a 10 000 euros
sources.supports: cash declaration threshold, scope and penalties

money-and-cost.rate_and_date: A$1 = 0.6293 EUR (Reserve Bank of Australia, 30 October 2026)
money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Cash declaration: French Customs requires anyone carrying cash, bearer negotiable instruments, prepaid cards or gold worth 10,000 euros or more (or the equivalent) to declare it, whether or not they live in France. 10,000 euros is about A$15,891 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026 (A$1 = EUR 0.6293). Amounts of 50,000 euros or more also need proof of where the money came from. Declare online (the DALIA service, up to 30 days ahead) or on a paper form. Failing to declare can bring a fine of up to 50% of the amount and seizure of the cash. The page doesn't name the French Southern and Antarctic Lands, so check with French Customs which form applies.
